verifiedAttackProposal.contract: Hard allowed, Risk frontier, complete purpose and PAC, post-fire escape, no greater counter exposure, response effect, and no committed EscapeObligation

exactRootCounterfactual.interpretation: the local attack-pose owner breaks strategic symmetry before the first eight-frame physical/star horizon exposes any value difference; terminal value depends on later target, resource, star-stream and opponent-response events

resourceAblation.interpretation: more FIRE obtained by deleting resource actions is strongly negative; bombs and poison are long-horizon options, not noise to suppress globally

eventDrivenOptionShadow.interpretation: semantic Option class changes without any external event in 21.89% of no-event frames, while frame-bound Plan signatures change on almost every callback; the current Plan identity cannot carry an attack objective across frames

stableOptionLedgerShadow.interpretation: semantic target-generation identity reuses an existing Option for 90.76% of tracked selections even though the primitive changes 1,480 times and frame-bound Plan signatures change 3,683 times inside the same generation; action and Plan identity are therefore invalid cross-frame Option keys

stableOptionIntervalShadow.interpretation: safe first-action attack evidence is not a multi-frame attack Option: only 38/99 event-bounded conflicts improve the balanced nominal rollout, current Risk never proves attackLower above incumbentUpper, and only one trajectory gains an enemy crash. Nominal terminal leaves remain full-range because the enemy policy is not universal.

attackContinuationProgressShadow.interpretation: the existing candidate set contains complete first steps but almost no attack continuation: 40/42 apparent improvements are reversible posture only, only 2/99 create durable progress, no generation preserves durable progress across two event revalidations, and both witnesses occur in matches V2 ultimately loses. The next step is a bounded attack-sequence generator, not activation or a looser certificate.

attackSequenceGeneratorShadow.interpretation: CURRENT emits no movement ATTACK_SETUP aliases, so the diagnostic generator scanned every Hard/Risk-frontier GO/TURN. A fixed common-policy setup-then-FIRE sequence is refuted immediately in all 296 candidates: one setup frame is insufficient to constrain the enemy or create hit progress. The required object is a bounded 2-4 frame observation-contingent attack policy, not a looser fixed sequence.

attackPolicyReachabilityShadow.contract: visible exact PhysicalState; Risk-frontier movement root; observation-contingent depth 2-4 AND/OR; every enemy action and ChanceOutcome; Hard at every successor; only enemy crash or real shield-hit closes movement progress; hidden, possible-projectile and incomplete support fail closed
attackPolicyReachabilityShadow.rejectedGoalDefinition: a debuff cast after arbitrary movement is root-independent because poison/stun are global; the initial 39 raw proofs were invalidated and retained only as a negative definition test
attackPolicyReachabilityShadow.interpretation: depth and budget are not the blocker: no movement root can force irreversible attack progress within four frames against every complete enemy response. Strict attack reachability remains Proof evidence only and cannot define ordinary ATTACK utility.

attackResponseSetShadow.contract: evaluate each enemy first action separately with the same strict continuation; compare complete constrained-response bitsets to the current action; only a strict superset without UNKNOWN is non-tradeoff evidence
attackResponseSetShadow.interpretation: the only two strictly constrained enemy columns belong to incumbent actions; every alternative movement constrains zero columns. Per-column proof nearly doubles local V2 runtime and is evidence-only, not a production search shape.

combatUtilityEnvelopeShadow.contract: keep elimination, pressure, mobility loss, endpoint reduction, counterfire delay, safety, resource and star opportunity cost as separate dimensions; apply opponent nominal policy plus recursive epsilon contamination; risk=100 retains one percent worst case
combatUtilityEnvelopeShadow.interpretation: risk-conditioned combat utility exists at ordinary attack roots, but it is almost always a cross-objective tradeoff: 97/99 attacks delay the cached star path and none dominates the incumbent across all dimensions. No weighted root FIRE score is entitled to action ownership.

riskConditionedCombatActive.contract: normal-mode STAR_CONTROL only; Hard/Risk/PAC complete FIRE; epsilon-contaminated offensive gain; no safety/counter-exposure regression; hit deadline no later than projected star deadline; four-frame physical survival and no immediate star loss
riskConditionedCombatActive.interpretation: an earlier attack deadline and bounded no-immediate-star-loss rollout increased FIRE but lost net outcomes. A primitive FIRE cannot replace a multi-frame STAR policy merely because local attack utility is positive.

attackStarPolicyFrontierShadow.contract: reuse the existing four-frame ATTACK and STAR policy continuations; compare survival, star gain/path, mobility, resource occupancy and combat progress as distinct Pareto dimensions; no new transition and no action ownership
attackStarPolicyFrontierShadow.interpretation: four-frame policy context eliminates every strict attack dominance candidate, but strict Pareto is also too conservative because all FIRE consumes a projectile resource and would delete known positive conversions. Tradeoff ownership needs a risk-conditioned Option policy value, not a new gate.

riskCombatCausalRoots.finding: positive and negative roots overlap on frame, star distance, endpoint reduction and local pressure. High pressure is concentrated in several negative roots; PAC response compression is therefore not durable attack progress and cannot be thresholded into an owner.

responseConditionedOptionPolicyShadow.contract: enumerate every exact enemy first response, continue ATTACK and STAR with state-conditioned policies for four frames, then back up eleven separate dimensions with OpponentModel probability and recursive epsilon contamination
responseConditionedOptionPolicyShadow.interpretation: explicit enemy responses make 18 additional roots risk-sensitive, but no aggregate ATTACK policy strictly dominates STAR. Stable-conflict roots do not align exactly with the one-shot proposal roots and therefore cannot classify the known terminal flips by themselves.

exactRiskCombatResponsePolicy.contract: evaluate the exact selected STAR row and exact risk-conditioned FIRE proposal row at the same restored root; incomplete observation, possible projectile and incomplete rollout fail closed
exactRiskCombatResponsePolicy.derivedQualification: complete support; nonloss, terminal and enemy-crash robust dimensions nonnegative; at least one strict combat improvement

responsePolicyActiveQualification.holdoutDiagnosis: local safety and combat improvement reduced aggregate self crashes but still sacrificed future star and position tempo. Both regressions occurred while already leading in stars and taking an attack policy with worse star-path progress; the one positive Holdout transition preserved star progress.

qualifiedAttackOverStarActive.contract: normal mode only; selected complete STAR_CONTROL; alternative Hard-allowed, Risk-frontier and purpose-complete ATTACK; committed EO, terminal mode, strict Proof and exact value remain higher owners
qualifiedAttackOverStarActive.interpretation: complete single-action attack evidence proves immediate legality, response effect and self-escape, but not that firing preserves the multi-frame kill sequence; more FIRE destroyed five net wins and reduced enemy crashes

nextArchitecture: generate ATTACK, RESOURCE, STAR_CONTROL and TERMINAL as separate event-bounded Options
bind every Option to target signature/generation, context epoch, deadline interval, abort events and response support
replace frame-bound attack and aim-setup signatures with stable target-generation identity before enabling persistence
use cached attack/star fields only as progress estimators inside an Option, never as cross-Option terminal value
keep Physical Hard and committed rescue on every emitted primitive
use bounded Minimax inside tactical Option response sets, not as the global objective selector
compare Options with terminal/nonloss interval and opportunity-cost vector before any local expected or tactical score
require an attack Option lower bound to exceed the competing Option upper bound; immediate self-escape and response compression are not sufficient
replan on observation, target, resource, committed-hazard or terminal events instead of every frame
require attack continuation progress across the stable generation before an ATTACK Option may challenge STAR_CONTROL or POSITION
treat deterministic multi-frame rollout as ordering evidence only; universal enemy/common-policy support is required for a strict interval
generate bounded attack continuations explicitly; do not activate the two sparse nominal witnesses or relax their certificate
keep 2-4 frame observation-contingent attack reachability as a strict certificate service only; it is empirically empty as ordinary movement ownership
define ordinary ATTACK with a multidimensional risk-conditioned combat utility (deadline, response compression, mobility denial, counter exposure and self-escape), not forced kill probability
apply recursive epsilon-contamination to the combat utility after Hard and Risk membership; ForcedWin and strict response elimination remain higher-priority sparse certificates
compare ATTACK and STAR as response-conditioned multi-frame policies; never substitute root FIRE for a long Option from deadline ordering alone
treat PAC pressure and endpoint reduction as local response evidence until the attack policy preserves durable progress across an event boundary
use strict Pareto only to remove dominated policy options; resolve real attack/star tradeoffs with the configured strategic risk profile, not another hard gate

separate strategic score-state bands from tactical risk: while leading, soft combat proposals may not spend verified star-path progress; tied/behind states may accept that tradeoff, but this rule requires a new unseen cohort before ownership
keep exact response-conditioned policy evaluation as a sparse evidence service; the Discovery-positive action owner failed the independent Holdout and remains disabled
